flashcards.q: What does KMP's lps[i] represent, and what does the whole array cost to build?
flashcards.a: Length of the longest proper prefix of pattern[0..i] that's also a proper suffix of it; built in O(m) amortized.

flashcards.q: On a KMP mismatch at pattern index j, what do you do and why does it never re-read text?
flashcards.a: Jump to j = lps[j-1] instead of resetting to 0; valid because pattern[0..lps[j-1]-1] is guaranteed to already match the text (it's a suffix of what just matched), so the text pointer never moves backward.

flashcards.q: What does the Z-array Z[i] represent?
flashcards.a: The length of the longest substring starting at i that matches a prefix of the whole string.

flashcards.q: Why must a Rabin-Karp hash match always be verified with an explicit character comparison?
flashcards.a: Hash collisions are possible (two different strings hashing to the same value mod M); skipping verification turns a probabilistic algorithm into one with real false positives.

flashcards.q: What is Rabin-Karp's worst-case complexity and when does it materialize?
flashcards.a: O(nm), same as naive search -- happens when many windows collide against the hash modulus, which an adversary can force if the modulus is small and fixed/known.

flashcards.q: How does lps[n-1] on a string (applied to itself) tell you if the string is periodic?
flashcards.a: If n % (n - lps[n-1]) == 0, the string has period (n - lps[n-1]) and is built from repeating that substring.

flashcards.q: Decision rule: exact match required, no hashing allowed vs multi-pattern fixed-window dedup -- which algorithm for each?
flashcards.a: Exact + no hashing -> KMP (or Z-algorithm). Multi-pattern / fixed-window dedup -> rolling hash (Rabin-Karp) with verification.

flashcards.q: What's the fix for Rabin-Karp's collision-attack vulnerability against a fixed, known modulus?
flashcards.a: Use a large randomly-seeded modulus chosen at process start, or double hashing with two independent base/modulus pairs, so an attacker can't precompute collisions offline.
